item.title: Michigan football to play both Tommy Carr, Bryce Underwood vs Oregon
item.description: Michigan football will play both Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood against Oregon today . Coach Kyle Whittingham said on the pregame radio the plan is for Carr, a true freshman, to start a fourth consecutive game, but U-M will bring Underwood into the game at some point. From there, whomever plays better could see the bulk of the snaps. "Tommy Carr will take the first snap," Whittingham told team play-by-play voice Doug Karsch before Saturday's kickoff. "You will see Bryce at some point in the game. Can't tell you exactly when because it's not scripted out, it's by feel. Then when they both start getting some action, if one of them is hot, we'll stick with that guy. "if not, we'll try to continue to get both playing Underwood was the starting quarterback through six games but was benched at halftime against Penn State after the Wolverines were shutout and turned the ball over twice in five drives. Carr came in for his first legitimate action in the second half and helped led the Wolverines to a comeback 21-18 victory. FOLLOW ALONG: Michigan football vs Oregon live updates, highlights He's since started the past three games − Indiana, Rutgers and Michigan State − but U-M is just 1-2 in those games and was shutout at halftime in both of the home starts. Underwood, meanwhile, has been a vocal and visible supporter of Carr on the sideline and remains a captain for the team. "His attitude through this whole thing has been terrific," Whittingham said. "You couldn't ask for more of a team guy, team mentality than what Bryce has demonstrated since we made the change. He practices hard, he's leading the team and everything in the warm-ups, you name it. He's you know acting as a captain should act, even though it's got to be very frustrating for him, and and has been a challenging time. "He couldn't have responded any better than he has, and we're really hoping that when he gets his opportunity, that he will make the most of it and have success." Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Email him at apgarcia@freepress.com and follow him on X at @RealTonyGarcia . item.title: Rice close to signing new Arsenal contract
item.description: Declan Rice joined Arsenal from West Ham in 2023 for £105m [Getty Images] Declan Rice has confirmed he is close to signing a new contract with Arsenal. BBC Sport first revealed the midfielder was set to sign a new long-term deal at Emirates Stadium on 7 October, and the 27-year-old, speaking before England's game against Spain on Sunday, said: "A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon and I'm extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust and team-mates who put so much energy in to me." Rice's current deal expires in 2028 but the former West Ham star is now expected to extended his tenure in north London, having arrived from London Stadium in 2023 in a deal worth £105m. The midfielder's new contract will put him alongside Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's top earner. Rice has managed to avoid upheaval during his career and he believes that continuity has helped him to blossom. "I've been extremely lucky I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career. I always set myself targets, pushing for more," he said. "I'm extremely Iucky not to have to worry about that stuff as it makes playing football far more easier." Latest Arsenal news, analysis and fan views Ask about Arsenal - what do you want to know?

item.title: Ohio State gets lift from RBs Bo Jackson, Isaiah West in win over Northwestern
item.description: Ohio State football snapped its losing skid with a 28-19 win over Northwestern on Nov. 14 at Ohio Stadium. The Buckeyes were 0-2 since returning from their off week, falling to USC and Oregon by more than 10 points in both games. Freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who has taken over for an injured Julian Sayin during this stretch, threw for 201 yards, three touchdowns and an interception in his first win as a starter. Former Ohio State offensive coordinator Chip Kelly was on the opposite sideline for the first time since winning the 2024 national championship with the Buckeyes. Northwestern's Kelly-ran offense posted 278 total yards while being held to two touchdowns and two field goals. Here are the game's key moments and takeaways: Ohio State's sophomore running back duo provides crucial production Sophomore running backs Bo Jackson and Isaiah West took on a large part of Ohio State's legwork, each finding the end zone and combining for 159 of the Buckeyes' 168 rushing yards. West rushed for 45 yards on 10 carries, and Jackson posted 114 rushing yards on 20 carries. Jackson was coming off a two-touchdown outing in the 41-28 loss to Oregon, though after scoring in the first quarter, he recorded just 17 yards the rest of the game. Against Northwestern, Jackson continued to be an asset following his 2-yard touchdown during the second quarter. Jeremiah Smith breaks Big Ten record early vs Northwestern Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith officially took the Big Ten all-time receiving yards title with a 22-yard catch near the end of the first quarter. Smith entered just 31 yards off from the record, which Purdue's John Standeford set at 3,788 in 2003. The record-breaking catch was the fourth of Smith's 11 receptions, a high in the three games Fahey has been at quarterback, and finished with 117 yards. In the fourth quarter, Smith logged his lone touchdown. He came close to scoring another in the second quarter, but instead had the first pass interference call go his way for the first time since the Purdue game last season. Northwestern defensive back Ore Adeyi was charged with the foul against Smith. Smith has the record at 3,874 yards with two games remaining in the regular season. A junior, Smith is likely in his final season at Ohio State, as he's expected to declare for the 2027 NFL Draft. Ohio State improves pass rush, third-down defense In the past two games, the Buckeyes' opponents had moved the chains 15 times on third down. The Wildcats did convert on third down six times, but their third-down conversion rate was below 40% (6 for 15). The biggest defensive boost Ohio State got against Northwestern was from the pass rush. After recording just two sacks across the past four games, the Buckeyes sacked Wildcats quarterback Nicco Marchiol five times, with Kenyatta Jackson Jr. leading the team with two. item.title: Golfer Tim O'Neal talks PGA diversity at Phoenix Charles Schwab Cup
item.description: Tim O'Neal had a calm smile during his practice shots at the Phoenix Country Club. Clad in his crisp blue long-sleeve shirt and Servpro badge, white hat and matching shorts, O'Neal was in the Valley competing in his third straight Charles Schwab Cup Championship, Nov. 12-15. O'Neal was among 36 qualifiers for the PGA Tour Champions season finale. He is the lone African-American competing for his first title. "Hopefully, other golfers of color will realize and see if I can do it, they can do it too," O'Neal told The Arizona Republic earlier this week. O'Neal is approaching nearly 30 years as a pro and fourth PGA Tour Champions season. He started on the Korn Ferry Tour as a rookie in 1997 out of Jackson State University, a rarity for a player from a historically Black college or university (HBCU). That was the same year Tiger Woods turned pro and became the first African-American to win the Masters. Since then, golf diversity has reached an all-time high of 25%, or seven million, among Black, Asian, or Latinx players in 2024, up from 8% in 1990, per the National Golf Foundation (NGF) and United States Golf Association (USGA). Black pro golfers also on the current tour include Harold Varner II, Joseph Bramlett and Cameron Champ. "With Tiger getting on tour, winning majors and dominating for a long time, that definitely I would think has had an effect," O'Neal said. O'Neal, 52, has had a strong 2026, with five top-10 finishes through 27 events. And he's still riding the coattails of his sole career victory at the Dominion Energy Charity Classic in October 2024. That's a turnaround from the multiple heartbreaks at qualifying school (Q-school) earlier in his career. He missed earning his PGA Tour card twice by one stroke in 2001 and 2004, before finally securing it in 2008. "You get a little smarter, course management's a little bit better," O'Neal said. "Probably in my younger days probably a little more aggressive on the course. I'm now a bit more conservative. ... But once I got on the Champions Tour, I think for me I still need some more work, but short game was the main thing. I've improved there but I still have some room to grow there as well and just getting more comfortable with these guys out here, some of the best players in the world." O'Neal was sponsored by actor and hip hop legend Will Smith earlier in his career. The loss of his PGA card, Nationwide Tour privileges and lack of money nearly caused O'Neal to quit for good. From 2010-11, O'Neal worked and gave lessons at Edwin Watts golf shop in his native Savannah, Georgia, while he played in mini tournaments over the next two years. His late mother Eva O'Neal, who passed away in 2020, urged him to stick with the game that she and his dad taught him to play. In 2013, O'Neal played in the eGOLF Tour in Charlotte, which helped jump-start his career. item.title: Declan Rice on ‘average’ World Cup, managing minutes and Graeme Souness criticism: ‘Football’s way different now’
item.description: As Declan Rice is discussing how he had an “average World Cup”, and talks at length about the challenges modern players have in ensuring prime fitness, a seemingly more trivial topic comes up: the punditry of Graeme Souness . The former Liverpool captain has in recent weeks criticised Rice for playing “old man’s football” and “cheating” in his midfield role, while insisting he’s a “centre-back”. Rice, of course, handles it diplomatically – “there would be no disrespect there, I’d shake his hand, I’d chat with him” – but with some edge, too. The England vice-captain asserts this is what the modern game demands, and it’s completely different to Souness’ time. “My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves,” Rice laughs, with a record of 15 goals and 25 assists in 129 Premier League appearances. “To be a top-class centre-back getting those numbers I’m delighted with that! The positioning, the ‘old man’s football’... look at Harry Kane . We played him the other week [ a 2-2 Arsenal draw at Bayern Munich ]. He dropped next to the centre-backs 20 to 30 times in the game to pick up the ball. The game’s different now. Rice has returned to the England midfield ahead of Sunday’s Nations League decider against Spain (Getty) “It's what the game demands, to get away from your man, to get away from who's marking you, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two-v-ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football's way different. You're always trying to look for tactical advantages.” Rice is essentially touching on a total transformation in football. Whereas “midfield generals” like Souness and even Roy Keane were able to fully impose themselves on a more loosely structured sport, their modern counterparts are now operating in a fully systemised game. And yet the issue of movement, and even “old man’s football”, also touches on something that is a bit raw – literally. Rice admits he is still “building up to being a 100 per cent” following the World Cup, and that only comes after a necessary intervention involving Thomas Tuchel . The 27-year-old missed England’s last camp after coming off in Arsenal’s 3-0 defeat to Brighton – their only dropped points this season – and admitting he “did not feel right at all on the pitch”. That came after a World Cup where he constantly suffered from hamstring pain, that radiated into his lower back, following a half-decade of constant football at the top level. “He [Tuchel] said, ‘Take some time, get yourself ready’,” Rice reveals. “It was using that time well to prepare to come back fitter, to come back stronger. item.title: 'One of the greatest wins' - Wales stun All Blacks to go from no-hopers to heroes
item.description: One of the greatest Wales wins of all time. That is how former captain Sam Warburton described the monumental result against New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday. At the time of the kick-off, the All Blacks were effectively the top-ranked side in the world following South Africa's tension-filled loss to France on Friday night. So no-one gave Wales hope - even Warburton - with some bookmakers offering odds of 30-1 during the week. The question, not of when but can, Wales beat the All Blacks again has beset them since 1953. That 73-year wait has been marred by cheating, national scandal and pure sporting drama. Little wonder then that few wanted to leave the Principality Stadium long after the final whistle had sparked unprecedented scenes of utter joy - and relief - to the strains of Yma O Hyd. That losing run - stretching across 34 matches - has hung like a millstone around the necks of generations of Wales players. Warburton himself was part of one of the most successful teams of all time during the Warren Gatland era - but lost all five meetings with New Zealand. Even the legendary team of the 1970s fell short, although Sir Gareth Edwards was among the Principality Stadium crowd on Saturday to witness history. How many more will claim in years to come that they were there as well? Wales believed they could create history - Lake All Blacks ran into a Welsh brick wall - Barrett Nations Championship: Wales end 73-year wait to beat New Zealand - reaction Warburton said: "When you think what the fans and this team has been through, from the highs of a Grand Slam seven years ago, down to 12th in the world rankings and a record losing run of any tier-one nation, we've been down in the pits. "No-one gave Wales a chance; that's why this is one of the greatest Welsh wins of all time. "Yes, New Zealand had made changes but that was one of the most heroic defensive performances I have ever seen." Dan Biggar, sat alongside Warburton for host broadcaster ITV, put the result into wider perspective. "This is not a day for analysis; it's just to celebrate being Welsh," he added. "That was probably the biggest shock in world rugby since Japan beat South Africa in the 2015 World Cup." item.title: Rutgers football's offense nonexistent in loss to Nebraska | Analysis
item.description: PISCATAWAY – This is the type of season it’s become for Rutgers football . The Scarlet Knights were already without starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan for Saturday’s game against Nebraska, and second-string quarterback AJ Surace was a game-time decision. Surace dressed and went through warmups, but third-stringer Sean Ashenfelder ultimately made his first career start. Then Ashenfelder suffered an apparent leg injury in the first half, and Surace had to come off the sideline and replace him. In a season that continues to spiral, the quarterback situation continues to worsen – the offense suffered a result. The Scarlet Knights got little going on that side of the ball, finishing with 143 total yards of offense in a 31-0 loss to the Cornhuskers at SHI Stadium. They had 101 rushing yards and averaged 3.1 yards per play. Greg Schiano’s team fell to 2-8 (1-6 Big Ten) with the loss – it has just two games to get through before it can officially begin a crucial offseason. But Rutgers still needs to get through those two games – at Penn State and home against Michigan State in the finale – and the mounting injuries continue to make it more difficult. The Scarlet Knights have already lost wide receiver KJ Duff, right guard Kobe Asamoah and safety Chris Joines for the season. This game wasn’t much of a fight – Nebraska, which secured its sixth win and bowl eligibility with a win that snapped a four-game losing streak, pretty much controlled it from the start and finished with 429 yards of offense. It was lopsided. But given the state of the Scarlet Knights right now, that shouldn’t come as much of a surprise, especially against a defense that ranks among the best in the Big Ten. Surace went 4-of-12 for 24 yards. Rutgers’ season is inching closer to a painful – literally – end. item.title: Zinedine Zidane responds to Kylian Mbappé rumours
item.description: Zinedine Zidane responds to Kylian Mbappé rumours France national team head coach Zinedine Zidane was this weekend drawn on the ongoing speculation, pointing towards a cold relationship between he and star striker Kylian Mbappé. The subject of the rapport between Zidane and Mbappé has dominated the media headlines in France across the week to date. This comes after it was rumoured that, not only were the pair not getting along, but they had endured a serious falling out during a training session. Speaking during an exchange with the media earlier this week, Mbappé for his part moved to firmly deny any and all rumours regarding as much. item.title: For Capitanes head coach Vitor Galvani, G League playoffs laid foundation for 2026-27
item.description: MEXICO CITY - At the start of the season after the Capitanes made the G League playoffs for the first time in franchise history, things are flowing smoother than usual as coach Vitor Galvani helps guide his ball club to a 3-1 start to their 2026-27 campaign. Not everything went well in the postseason, which Galvani is the first to admit, but it also helped build a foundation to continue the upward trajectory of the Mexican franchise. "It's not that we gave up when we got to the playoffs, but honestly, I take the blame for this," said the Capitanes coach (translation ours). "We didn't have the mindset of 'let's play until the 15th,' which is when you become champions." And while an early exit in the G League playoffs was by no means a desired outcome, it also prepared the team for this campaign. "It gives us more confidence in some areas," he continued. "Last year, we came in with several ideas about how we wanted to play offensively and defensively. And I think we got 70 percent of it right; the other 30 percent had to change over the course of the season." "I feel more confident about doing that 70 percent better this year," said Galvani. "At times last year, there were moments when we wondered if this going to work or not, we have more confidence in that now." "Last year, I told you that our goal was to make the playoffs," said the Capitanes coach. "Now I want to fight for more because I feel confident in our staff and our players, and that we can do it. Now, I don’t know, maybe it’s the other way around." "This league that you already know, in one week we could have three NBA players (join a team), and everything changes. So, it’s about controlling what’s within our control. Doing the training we did today, with lots of energy, really wanting to improve, wanting to talk to one another, and from there, gradually achieving things." item.title: Mets Lock In Devin Williams As Closer For 2027 Season
item.description: Aug 7, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; New York Mets relief pitcher Devin Williams (38) pitches against the Pittsburgh Pirates during the ninth inning at PNC Park. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The New York Mets are not looking for a new closer. They have already decided that Devin Williams will anchor the ninth inning in 2027. According to Rising Apple , the team views Williams as the man to finish games and is now hunting for high-leverage arms to support him. This is a clear shift from the chaos of the past year. The front office knows exactly what it wants, and it is not a mystery. Pat Ragazzo of Rising Apple reported that the club is targeting relievers who can handle the seventh and eighth innings. These are the critical spots that set up Williams. The Mets traded away A.J. Minter, Brooks Raley, Luke Weaver, and Huascar Brazobán at the trade deadline. Those moves left a hole, but the team has a specific plan to fill it. They are looking at left-handers like Alex Vesia and Tim Hill. They have also checked in on Minter and Raley again. Even free-agent right-hander Jonathan Loáisiga has drawn interest. Getting Guys Out Is All That Matters Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns made his stance clear at the GM Meetings in Las Vegas. He told reporters that the team does not care about handedness or past roles. “It’s really ‘can we just get guys out?'” Earlier in the week, Stearns spoke to reporters at GM Meetings . He added that whether a pitcher is right-handed or left-handed is “a little bit less important for us.” This is a refreshing take. Too many teams get hung up on matchups instead of just finding guys who can retire batters. Williams brings his own challenges to the table . Last season, he recorded a 4.43 ERA and a 1.57 WHIP across 44 appearances. In August, a right shoulder strain placed him on the injured list. He returned in late September to finish the year. Despite the rough ERA, the underlying numbers show promise. Against him, opponents swung and missed on 34.4% of their attempts. Baseball Savant put his expected ERA at 3.22. The Mets are betting on that ability to miss bats, not just the surface stats. Money and Roster Spots Drive the Offseason The financial commitment to Williams is significant. He signed a three-year deal worth $51 million last winter. The agreement includes a $6 million signing bonus. With two seasons left on that contract, the Mets have no reason to look elsewhere for the closer role. The real work is finding the bridge pitchers to get to him. Stearns has to clear six roster spots to protect seven prospects before the lockout hits on Dec. 2. Players like Jefferson Rojas and Jack Wenninger face risk if the team does not act fast. The lockout could freeze all transactions until a new deal is reached. If the draft happens, the Mets could lose a young player they need for depth. The Miami Dolphins (1-7) have made three roster moves ahead of their Week 10 road matchup against the Indianapolis Colts (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, adding kicker Zane Gonzalez, quarterback Brady Cook and wide receiver Jalen Reagor to their active roster. He also connected on two of three attempts against the New England Patriots in Week 8, making another 52-yard field goal. The Dolphins had exhausted Gonzalez’s three permitted practice squad elevations, making his signing to the active roster necessary for him to continue handling kicking duties. item.title: Bryson DeChambeau Builds His Legacy Back Home In Clovis
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Bryson DeChambeau is building an 18-hole golf course and a residential community right in his hometown of Clovis, California, according to Billionaires.Africa . The two-time U.S. Open champion announced this massive project on Friday, November 13. He plans to turn the historic McFarlane Ranch into a hub for golf and living. The project covers about 200 acres on the northeastern edge of Fresno. DeChambeau expects the city to approve the plan within 18 months. He told reporters that a significant portion of his LIV Golf earnings is being allocated to finance this development. His contract with the Saudi-backed league was widely reported at about $125 million when he joined in 2022. That financial backing allows him to reshape his local landscape without waiting for outside investors. Most golf stars chase fame in big cities like Los Angeles or Miami. DeChambeau is doing the opposite by investing in a city of about 120,000 people. He grew up in Clovis and attended Clovis East High School before turning pro. The plan pairs the new golf course with homes for people to buy. It creates a long-term legacy rather than a quick profit flip. With five LIV Golf titles to his name, DeChambeau has secured nine victories during his PGA Tour career. He also has two major championships to his name. His scientific approach to the game made him one of the most talked-about players ever. Now he is applying that same focus to building a community. His academic path included studying physics at Southern Methodist University, where he claimed the 2015 NCAA individual title. That same drive for precision is now being used to design a course and a neighborhood. The Content King Builds Real Things On his YouTube channel, DeChambeau boasts a subscriber count exceeding three million. His fame in content creation matches the renown he has achieved through his competitive career. While other players focus on social media clips, he is building something you can walk on. The Head Professional at Sugarloaf Golf Club, Oscar Parks, said DeChambeau is very down to earth. Parks noted that the group did not have a ton of lists or demands during their time together. “They were very professional and they didn’t waste a lot of time,” Parks explained in an interview. He further noted that the group consisted entirely of ordinary guys. This attitude fits the Clovis project perfectly. DeChambeau does not need a fancy clubhouse to prove his worth. He needs a place where he can play and build with people he knows.

item.title: Ancelotti sees red in Brazil’s defeat to Japan: ‘The referee lacked experience’
item.description: Ancelotti sees red in Brazil’s defeat to Japan: ‘The referee lacked experience’ Carlo Ancelotti blamed an inexperienced referee after he was sent off during Brazil’s 3-2 friendly defeat to Japan in Singapore. Japan took a 2-0 lead inside the first 20 minutes at the National Stadium through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura. Vinícius Júnior scored twice to level the game, and Endrick, who’s being linked with Roma and Milan, hit the crossbar with the score at 2-2. Japan then scored a winner in stoppage time. Brazil felt João Gomes had been fouled in the build-up, and Ancelotti ran onto the pitch to protest and was sent off by Singaporean referee Jansen Foo Chuan Hui. Raphinha was also dismissed for protesting from the bench. “The result was clearly affected by the referee, who wasn’t able to control the game,” Ancelotti said, with quotes via IlNapolista . “But it isn’t really his fault. This was a high-level game, and I don’t think he had the experience to handle a match like this. “He showed me a red card because he said I wasn’t able to control my bench, since the players were on the pitch.” PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – JUNE 19: Carlo Ancelotti, Head Coach of Brazil, looks on before the FIFA World Cup 2026 Group C match between Brazil and Haiti at Philadelphia Stadium on June 19, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Dan Mullan/Getty Images) Ancelotti on Brazil’s performance The CBF’s national teams director, Rodrigo Caetano, also criticised the appointment. For away friendlies, FIFA chooses the referee at the request of the home federation, which in this case was Japan. Ancelotti admitted his side started poorly but felt they deserved more. “The first part wasn’t good. The defensive line didn’t move well, we tried to press high and it didn’t work,” he said. “After the 20th minute, the team created chances and played well with the ball, and I’m satisfied with that part. We played with rhythm and intensity, and we could have won. It’s a shame about the result, because I don’t like losing, but we have to look at the good things we did.” EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY – JUNE 13: Carlo Ancelotti, Head Coach of Brazil, reacts after the 1-1 draw during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Group C match between Brazil and Morocco at New York New Jersey Stadium on June 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. item.title: Former Arizona WR Braylen Ross flipped his commitment to Oklahoma State
item.description: Irvine (Calif.) Crean Lutheran wide-out Braylen Ross has flipped his commitment from Arizona to Oklahoma State . Ross committed to the Wildcats back in May but took an official visit to Oklahoma State over Halloween weekend. He told us he loved everything about the visit, felt at home and decided to flip his commitment to the Cowboys earlier today. “I fell in love with the school on that visit,” Ross said. “I loved everything about it and obviously really like the football program. They have a great offense that features the passing game and I think it’s a great all around fit for me. “I was there for Homecoming weekend and the game atmosphere and fan support were incredible. That visit really opened my eyes and exceeded my expectations. I had never been to a game and seen fan support like that. It was honestly like nothing I’ve ever seen before.” Ross said his relationship with the coaches played a big role. “I really like the coaching staff,” Ross said. “They made me feel like I was a high priority ever since they offered me back in September. I felt a really strong connection with everyone there and especially Coach Morris and Coach Edwards. “It wasn’t an easy decision, and these types of things are never easy. I had a lot of respect for the Arizona staff, but I really felt like this was the best decision for me and I’m looking forward to becoming a college athlete at Oklahoma State.” Ross had a breakout season at Crean Lutheran after transferring in from San Diego (Calif.) Lincoln over the Spring. He had to sit out his junior season at Lincoln due to some eligibility issues but flashed at several camps and 7v7 events and looked primed for a strong senior year. “I know there are some guys rated higher but for me, he’s not just one of the best receivers in California; he’s one of the best in the entire region, Malik James of James Sports Group said. “He’s tall, he’s physical, has big hands, has a high end skill set, and great body control. “On top of that, he’s a great kid with a great personality. “I like everything about him and I think he’s a great pickup for Oklahoma State.”

item.title: Austin Cindric Wins Veterans Classic At Daytona Beach
item.description: Robert Noaker (13) and Austin Cindric (2) race to the start/finish line during the Veterans Day Classic on Nov. 11, 2026, at Daytona International Speedway. Austin Cindric proved he can still win at Daytona Beach on Wednesday night. At the first Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic, he claimed the checkered flag. This 30-minute exhibition race featured 12 Ford-affiliated drivers in Mustang Dark Horse Rs. Cindric started from the pole and held off a fierce late challenge from Robert Noaker. The pair swapped the lead three times in the final minutes before Cindric made the winning pass. Noaker, who represents the Marine Corps, finished second. Ryan Preece took third for the Navy. Cindric joked about his win in Victory Lane, saying, according to Speedway Digest , “I finally have something to put on the center of the Christmas card, so I did win a race this year after all the talk.” He noted that the event was a great way to honor the veterans and the Air Force. A Clean Battle for Military Bragging Rights The race had no championship points, but the bragging rights were huge for the military branches. It was a rare sight in stock car racing to see such close driving end safely. Noaker said he knew Cindric would race clean, and it was fun to compete that close. “It was a blast to race Austin,” Noaker said. “I knew he was gonna race clean. He probably knew I was gonna race clean and it was so much fun to race that close and not have any contact and put on a great show for all the veterans here tonight.” This clean finish showed that respect matters more than just winning the trophy. More History Coming to the Sands Very few races remain at the World Center of Racing that Cindric has not won. He admitted he still wants to conquer the truck race and the Rolex 24. “There’s only two races at Daytona I’ve entered, this is a subtle brag, that I haven’t won and it’s the truck race and it’s the Rolex 24,” Cindric said. While Cindric chases his next win, the track prepares for a massive historic return. The legendary Sunbeam 1000hp will come back to Daytona Beach in 2027. On those sands, Sir Henry Segrave set a world land speed record of 203.792 mph, an event marking 100 years. The car is coming back after a three-year restoration by the National Motor Museum. Jon Murden, Chief Executive of the museum, said, according to SpeedwayMedia.com , “To be able to take this iconic car back to Daytona Beach, where World Land Speed Record history was made, will be incredible – especially in the centenary year.” On Saturday at 2:00 p.m., the HSR Classic Daytona 24 Hour presented by Mission Foods begins.
